answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity like pigment in a prism: each agent must lock a small, time-vested stake before its attestations count, and that stake only grows through verified work. Newcomers climb a slow spiral of trust, where peers check past deeds before weighting their votes, so a flood of fresh clones stays powerless: clones begin with zero standing, and standing is earned one attested contribution at a time, never bought in bulk.
